children: This summit occurred at a pivotal time when India aims to reduce its dependence on imports, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and enhance capabilities across emerging sectors

The seventh edition of BW Future of Design, held in September 2026 in Mumbai, brought together designers, architects, brand leaders, and industry practitioners to explore how design can contribute to building a self-reliant India. The theme, "Designing for a Self-Reliant India," emphasised design as a catalyst for innovation, manufacturing, digital infrastructure, and future-ready solutions.

This summit occurred at a pivotal time when India aims to reduce its dependence on imports, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and enhance capabilities across emerging sectors. With a youthful population and a growing focus on skill development and education, the event examined how design can transform these advantages into products, technologies, and experiences that meet the country's evolving needs.

The awards recognised and honoured the best prototypes and finished designs that demonstrate relevance, innovation, and the ability to address changing needs. This initiative showcased products and design solutions from various industries, highlighting the increasing importance of design in shaping products and experiences that impact everyday lives.

The awards also highlighted designs that could contribute to a future-ready India. From products and technologies to brands, spaces, and user experiences, the recognition celebrated work that illustrates how design can facilitate innovation while responding to shifting economic, social, and industrial requirements.

The seventh edition of BW Future of Design featured an experienced jury of leaders from design, branding, architecture, automotive, technology, and creative industries. The panel was chaired by Pradyumna Vyas, President of the World Design Organisation (WDO), and included Annurag Batra, Chairman & Editor-in-Chief of BW Businessworld; V. Sunil, Design Thinker and Brand Architect, Co-founder of Motherland, and Founding Trustee of the Kochi Biennale Foundation; Geet Nazir, Managing Director of Landor; and Ajay Jain, Head of Design Studio at Tata Motors.

The panel also comprised Mohan Krishnaraj, Global Head of Design, Product and Studios at Cognizant Moment; Sonali Bhagwati, Partner at Designplus Architecture; David Abraham, Creative Director at Abraham & Thakore; Rakesh Thakore, Creative Director at Abraham & Thakore; and Preeti Vyas, Chairwoman & Founder of Vyas Giannetti Creative.

The jury evaluated recognised designs across product design, mobility, architecture, branding, technology, fashion, and creative practice, reflecting the awards’ focus on creativity, purpose, execution, and real-world relevance. The Future of Design platform underscores design approaches that connect innovation with functionality, showcasing the role of design in shaping contemporary business, industry, and everyday experiences.
The author is a Trainee Content Writer at BW Businessworld. He is an English Journalism graduate from IIMC, New Delhi.
